Run the CATE simulation grid

Source: R/sim-cate-run.R
sim_cate_run.Rd

Expands a grid of DGP designs, sample sizes, and covariate dimensions, then runs n_reps independent Monte Carlo replications for each cell using sim_cate_one_rep(). Each replicate draws one dataset and evaluates all requested methods on the same draw, enabling like-for-like comparisons. Returns a tidy data.frame of raw per-replicate, per-method results. Use summarise_sim_results() to aggregate to one row per (method, design, n, kx, candidate_id, lambda, s).

Usage

sim_cate_run(
  designs = c("dgp1_linear", "dgp2_nonlinear", "dgp3_sparse_overlap", "dgp4_clustered",
    "dgp5_correlated"),
  n_vals = c(500L, 1000L, 2000L),
  kx_vals = 2L,
  n_reps = 500L,
  master_seed = 42L,
  k = 1L,
  s_fn = function(n, kx) floor(0.4 * n^((kx + 1L)/(kx + 2L))),
  tuning = NULL,
  tuning_mode = c("default", "grid"),
  methods = "dnn_oracle",
  alpha = 0.05,
  sigma = 0.5,
  clip = 0.001,
  n_folds = 5L,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

designs

Character vector of DGP names.

n_vals

Integer vector of sample sizes.

kx_vals

Integer vector of covariate dimensions.

n_reps

Number of Monte Carlo replications per cell.

master_seed

Integer seed used to draw the per-replicate seeds. Every cell uses the same seed vector so noise realisations are comparable across DGPs, sample sizes, and methods (fair comparison).

k

Integer DNN neighbour count. The paper-facing DNN default is k = 1L, meaning one nearest neighbor is selected inside each size-s subsample; larger values use the package's generalized top-k weights. The fixed-k extension is essentially direct, but the current paper derivations are written for k = 1.

s_fn

Function f(n, kx) returning the integer kernel order. The finite-sample default is \(s = \lfloor 0.4 n^{(k_x+1)/(k_x+2)} \rfloor\).

tuning

Optional kernel-order tuning specification. When supplied, s is resolved per simulation cell from tuning_eval(..., mode = "default") and s_fn must be omitted.

tuning_mode

One of "default" or "grid". "default" preserves scalar simulation behavior. "grid" requires tuning; DNN methods emit one row per tuning candidate from the integrated cate_dnn() grid payload, while non-DNN benchmarks emit one row with candidate_id = NA and s = NA.

methods

Character vector of method names; see sim_cate_methods(). Default: "dnn_oracle".

alpha

Nominal coverage level.

sigma

Noise SD forwarded to the DGP.

clip

Propensity clipping bound forwarded to the DGP and cross-fitting.

n_folds

Number of cross-fitting folds for the dnn_crossfit method.

verbose

Print one progress line per cell (default TRUE).

Value

A data.frame with raw rows and columns method, design, n, kx, k, tuning_source, candidate_id, lambda, s, seed, tau_hat, tau0, bias, sq_err, se, cover, ci_len, neff, method_variant, forest_nuisance, y_hat_supplied, and w_hat_supplied, plus the localization and studentization diagnostics described in sim_cate_one_rep() and status. The GRF fields identify whether the forest used oracle nuisances ("oracle"), common externally estimated nuisances ("common_external"), or internally estimated nuisances ("internal"), and whether Y.hat and W.hat were supplied. Non-GRF methods carry typed missing values for these fields. Failed entries have NA for all metric columns.

Parallelism

When the future.apply package is installed, the rep loop within each cell is parallelised via future.apply::future_lapply(). Control the backend by calling future::plan() before sim_cate_run():

# All local cores (PC or single SLURM node):
future::plan(future::multisession)
raw <- sim_cate_run(...)

Without future.apply the function falls back silently to sequential lapply. For multi-node HPC, see system.file("paper-replication/cate/hpc", package = "RdistNN").

Fault tolerance

Each replicate is wrapped in tryCatch. A total rep failure (e.g. DGP draw error) records NA for all metrics and all methods and emits a warning; per-method failures are handled inside sim_cate_one_rep(). Registered GRF route metadata is retained in both replacement paths. summarise_sim_results() reports n_failed per candidate-aware group.

See also

sim_cate_one_rep(), summarise_sim_results(), sim_cate_methods()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Single method (default):
raw <- sim_cate_run(designs = "dgp2_nonlinear", n_vals = 500L, n_reps = 10L)

# Multiple methods on the same draws:
future::plan(future::multisession)
raw <- sim_cate_run(
  designs = "dgp2_nonlinear", n_vals = 500L, n_reps = 10L,
  methods = c("dnn_fullsample", "dnn_crossfit", "ols_interact", "causal_forest")
)
future::plan(future::sequential)

summarise_sim_results(raw)
} # }
